articles.title: Is Tommy McMillen the UFC’s Next Superstar?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Could Tommy “Gun” McMillen become the second-biggest star in UFC history? Conor McGregor remains the standard, but determining who belongs directly behind him is more complicated. Georges St-Pierre produced enormous pay-per-view numbers. Paddy Pimblett has become a massive attraction. Ilia Topuria, Islam Makhachev, Sean O’Malley, Ronda Rousey and Jon Jones all have arguments depending on how stardom is measured. Chael Sonnen believes McMillen could eventually surpass nearly all of them. Tommy has the fighting ability, an authentic personality and the rare ability to deliver a promotional line without making it sound rehearsed. He also trains alongside O’Malley under Tim Welch, giving him access to people who understand that becoming a star requires more than winning fights. McMillen’s undefeated record survived another major test at Noche UFC when he defeated Marwan Rahiki by unanimous decision in a back-and-forth fight. Instead of exposing Tommy, the adversity allowed him to demonstrate toughness, composure and the ability to close strongly. There are still questions. Tommy must continue winning, reach numbered UFC events and discover what will motivate him once the money and attention arrive. But right now, Chael sees no evidence that disqualifies him from becoming the UFC’s next transcendent superstar. articles.title: Tom Vacated. Does Jon Jones Come Back?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartnerTom Aspinall has vacated the UFC heavyweight championship, making Ciryl Gane the biggest winner in the division. But this story may be more complicated than it first appears. After Gane’s disappointing loss to Jon Jones, another opportunity to become undisputed champion appeared almost impossible. The UFC had no interest in booking that rematch. Somehow, Gane worked his way back, defeated Alex Pereira for the interim title and now stands as the undisputed heavyweight champion. Chael Sonnen explains why Gane’s career looks completely different today. His close fight with Francis Ngannou carries more weight, his championship résumé continues to grow and the dangerous fighter who emerged from the White House event may be better than anyone realized. Tom’s departure also creates another possibility: could Jon Jones come back? Jones never seemed interested in facing Aspinall. But would he return for a championship fight against an opponent he has already defeated? Chael examines whether Gane’s rise could reopen the door for Jones, what that would mean for Josh Hokit and why another Jon Jones title reign could create even more problems for the heavyweight division. Is Ciryl Gane the biggest winner from Tom Aspinall vacating, or does this situation benefit Jon Jones even more? articles.title: Tom Aspinall Vacates UFC Heavyweight Title
articles.description: Tom Aspinall has officially vacated the UFC heavyweight championship after ongoing complications with his eyes prevented him from receiving medical clearance. Aspinall revealed that he had agreed to a fight date, returned to sparring and felt ready to compete. Then another accident caused further damage to his right eye. Rather than continue holding up the heavyweight division, Tom made the difficult decision to relinquish the title. Chael Sonnen reacts to Aspinall’s deeply personal statement and acknowledges that the MMA community, including Chael himself, did not understand how serious the situation had become. But Tom’s announcement also creates a major development that many headlines are overlooking. With Aspinall stepping aside, interim champion Ciryl Gane is positioned as the undisputed UFC heavyweight champion. The question now becomes who gets the first opportunity against him. Does Josh Hokit’s aggressive campaign earn him the fight? Could Alex Pereira receive another opportunity? Or will Alexander Volkov finally enter the conversation? Chael breaks down Tom’s decision, Ciryl Gane’s new position and the battle to become the UFC’s next heavyweight title challenger. articles.title: Ilia Topuria Wants Justin Gaethje, NOW!
articles.description: Ilia Topuria wants an immediate rematch with Justin Gaethje, and Chael Sonnen doesn't understand the resistance. Topuria was an undefeated champion and the favorite before Gaethje pulled off the upset. With the rest of the lightweight division still sorting itself out, Chael believes Topuria remains one of the most logical options for Gaethje's next title defense. Gaethje has publicly said he doesn't want rematches. He wants new names and new experiences before his career ends. But Chael doesn't believe that means Gaethje would actually turn Topuria down if the UFC made the call. Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy still have business to settle. Usman Nurmagomedov isn't in the UFC yet. Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira have their own complications. Start eliminating the alternatives, and Chael keeps coming back to the same name. articles.title: Why did Usman turn down $2 million? #ufc
articles.description: Why would Kamaru Usman turn down a $2 million offer from the PFL? Chael Sonnen says that decision raises some serious questions. Chael breaks down Usman’s situation and explains why the UFC’s current “offer” may actually be silence. Is Usman betting on a bigger opportunity, or is money simply not the priority? For Chael, there’s another factor that can completely change the equation: the fight itself. A rivalry, a grudge, a social-media feud, or one heated exchange can be worth more than millions of dollars when it creates a fight people actually want to see. So what is Usman waiting for — and does the UFC have the right fight for him? #UFC #MMA #KamaruUsman #ChaelSonnen #PFL #UFCNews #MMAnews

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Is Ready to Fight!
articles.description: Ilia Topuria is ready to fight again, and Chael Sonnen believes the lightweight title picture is beginning to point toward a rematch with Justin Gaethje. Gaethje has said he doesn't want another rematch and may not compete again until 2027. But Dana White recently made it clear that he believes Gaethje still has plenty of fights and money left on the table. That creates a problem. Topuria isn't the only elite lightweight Gaethje has already faced. Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira have beaten him as well. If Gaethje remains champion, Chael argues that simply refusing rematches can't prevent legitimate contenders from earning title opportunities. And if Topuria competes again and wins, Chael believes his position becomes especially difficult to deny There are still other possibilities, including the winner of Arman Tsarukyan vs. Mauricio Ruffy. But after listening to Gaethje, Topuria and Dana White, Chael sees the wind blowing in one direction: Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria, Part 2. articles.title: Tommy Gunn's Hotel Confrontation
articles.description: Tommy Gunn ran into his UFC Noche opponent at the fighter hotel, and things quickly got uncomfortable. What started as a conversation turned into both fighters refusing to give ground. Tommy didn't want his opponent anywhere near him. His opponent couldn't understand why Tommy was reacting that way. Eventually, they let each other get close enough that Chael Sonnen believes they broke one of the most important rules of a confrontation outside the Octagon. If someone with bad intentions gets within range, the situation has already changed. But Chael noticed something else while watching the video: everyone had their phones out, everyone was watching, and Tommy had an entourage around him. What he didn't have was the one person every fighter needs in exactly this situation. articles.title: You Have No Idea How Big Islam Is in Russia
articles.description: Chael Sonnen just returned from Russia with Real American Freestyle, and some of the most memorable moments had nothing to do with what happened in competition. Chael wanted to understand how Russians view their combat sports legends. Alexander Karelin is one of the greatest wrestlers ever. Fedor Emelianenko became an MMA icon. But when Chael asked a Russian about Khabib Nurmagomedov, the reaction was completely different. Then there was Khamzat Chimaev honoring wrestling legend Buvaisar Saitiev after his match, and Islam Makhachev creating such a scene that simply moving him through the building required armed security. Yet Islam still stopped for fans, kids and photographs as he was being escorted out. Chael saw firsthand how these fighters are received when they return to Russia and what wrestling and fighting mean within that culture. And before the night ended, Jordan Burroughs called out Islam Makhachev, bringing an old challenge back to life. articles.title: Ilia vs. Gaethje 2 Is the RIGHT Fight #ufc
articles.description: Does Ilia Topuria really need to rebuild his way back to the UFC title? Chael Sonnen says absolutely not. Ilia was an undefeated champion, a heavy favorite, and one of the biggest stars in the UFC when Justin Gaethje handed him the upset loss. Now the question is whether Ilia should fight his way back up the division — or immediately get another shot at the belt. Chael argues that Ilia vs. Gaethje 2 isn't just a good idea. It's the right idea. And there's another problem with making Ilia “rebuild”: the possible opponents waiting for him have already proven themselves against the current champion. Chael explains why putting Ilia against a lesser-ranked opponent could actually create an even more dangerous fight. Should Ilia get an immediate rematch with Justin Gaethje? Or does he need to earn his way back? #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #UFCRematch
